q: (Do not forget the Day of Qiyaamah)
v.s: When the sun is wrapped up [in darkness]
v.c: When the sun is put out,

v.s: And when the stars fall, dispersing,
v.c: and when the stars fall down,

q: When the mountains are made to fly about
(like flakes of wool after being flung into the air by violent earthquakes).
v.s: And when the mountains are removed
v.c: and when the mountains are blown away,

q: (by their owners). (Although pregnant camels are highly prized and valuable, people will have no interest in them or in any other valuables when the fear of Qiyaamah overwhelms them.)
v.s: And when full-term she-camels are neglected
v.c: and when pregnant camels are left untended,

q: (together on the Plains of Reckoning so that oppressed animals are given the opportunity to take revenge from the aggressors).
v.s: And when the wild beasts are gathered
v.c: and when wild beasts are gathered together,

q: When the oceans are set alight
(to boil). (The waters of the ocean will be heated so intensely that, all the water will evaporate and fire will then take its place.)
v.s: And when the seas are filled with flame
v.c: and when the seas are set on fire,

q: (After the Kuffaar are separated from the Mu'mineen, the members of each group of Kuffaar and each group of Mu'mineen will come together.)
v.s: And when the souls are paired
v.c: and when the souls ˹and their bodies˺ are paired ˹once more˺,

q: When the girl buried alive will be asked...
v.s: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked
v.c: and when baby girls, buried alive, are asked

q: Of or what sin she was killed.
(These two verses refer to the practice of some Arab Mushrikeen during the period of ignorance who used to bury their infant daughters alive merely because they disliked having daughters.)
v.s: For what sin she was killed
v.c: for what crime they were put to death,

q: (for) scrutiny and for judgement to be passed).
v.s: And when the pages are spread [i.e., made public]
v.c: and when the records ˹of deeds˺ are laid open,

q: When the sky will be opened,
v.s: And when the sky is stripped away
v.c: and when the sky is stripped away,

q: (prepared to receive the Kuffaar and sinners).
v.s: And when Hellfire is set ablaze
v.c: and when the Hellfire is fiercely flared up,

q: When Jannah will be brought close
(to the pious Mu'mineen so that they look forward to it).
v.s: And when Paradise is brought near,
v.c: and when Paradise is brought near—

q: On that day every soul will know what
(committed and which is now revealed for judgment).
v.s: A soul will [then] know what it has brought [with it].
v.c: ˹on that Day˺ each soul will know what ˹deeds˺ it has brought along.

q: I swear by the planets that recede
(which set on the horizon as the stars do)...
v.s: So I swear by the retreating stars -
v.c: I do swear by the receding stars

q: (disappear from sight as the night fades).
v.s: Those that run [their courses] and disappear [i.e., set]
v.c: which travel and hide,

v.s: And by the night as it closes in
v.c: and the night as it falls

q: ...and by the morning when it takes a breath
v.s: And by the dawn when it breathes [i.e., stirs]
v.c: and the day as it breaks!

v.s: [That] indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is a word [conveyed by] a noble messenger [i.e., Gabriel]
v.c: Indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is the Word of ˹Allah delivered by Gabriel,˺ a noble messenger-angel,

q: ...who is powerful and of high rank
in the sight of the Owner of the Throne.
v.s: [Who is] possessed of power and with the Owner of the Throne, secure [in position],
v.c: full of power, held in honour by the Lord of the Throne,

q: (and will therefore never corrupt any message Allaah sends with him).
v.s: Obeyed there [in the heavens] and trustworthy.
v.c: obeyed there ˹in heaven˺, and trustworthy.

v.s: And your companion [i.e., Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ] is not [at all] mad.
v.c: And your fellow man is not insane.

v.s: And he has already seen him [i.e., Gabriel] in the clear horizon.
v.c: And he did see that ˹angel˺ on the clear horizon,

q: He is also not miserly with the knowledge of the unseen.
(Rasulullaah ﷺ conveyed to the people whatever knowledge of the unseen Allaah taught him without demanding a fee as fortune-tellers do.)
v.s: And he [i.e., Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم)] is not a withholder of [knowledge of] the unseen.
v.c: and he does not withhold ˹what is revealed to him of˺ the unseen.

q: the word of any accursed Shaytaan.
v.s: And it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is not the word of a devil, expelled [from the heavens].
v.c: And this ˹Quran˺ is not the word of an outcast devil.

v.s: So where are you going?
v.c: So what ˹other˺ path would you take?

q: is but a great advice to the
v.s: It is not except a reminder to the worlds
v.c: Surely this ˹Quran˺ is only a reminder to the whole world—

q: ...for those of you who wish to walk the straight path.
v.s: For whoever wills among you to take a right course.
v.c: to whoever of you wills to take the Straight Way.

q: without the will of Allaah the Rabb of the universe.
(Therefore, a person can tread the straight path only when Allaah permits him, and this occurs only when he sincerely expresses the desire to do so.)
v.s: And you do not will except that God wills - Lord of the worlds.
v.c: But you cannot will ˹to do so˺, except by the Will of Allah, the Lord of all worlds.
